children: rose 7.6% in late Wednesday morning trading as investors digested the company's second-quarter earnings report. For their part, analysts weighed in favorably on the update.
William Blair analyst Sharon Zackfia noted that Jersey Mike's

second quarter met the range provided during the IPO runup, and comparable sales continued to accelerate into the third quarter. "Given its relatively unique status as a franchisor with strong expansion prospects, we view Jersey Mike’s premium valuation to other franchisors as warranted at an enterprise value of 20 times our 2027 EBITDA estimate, in keeping with the average of other high-growth restaurant brands," updated Zackfia. William Blair kept its Outperform rating on JMKE in place on the expectation for low-teens profit growth with potential upside to yield healthy stock appreciation.
RBC Capital Markets analyst Logan Reich noted Jesey Mike's

reported second-quarter earnings largely in line with the previously disclosed metrics in the S-1. The report was solid enough for the firm to keep its Outperform rating on JMKE and price target of $28.00 in place.

Wells Fargo analyst Zachary Fadem called the second quarter results largely positive. "The JMKE story is strong, Q2 traffic growth is encouraging & 2H upside is likely via share gains & ample initiatives (LTOs, loyalty, etc.)," he wrote. The firm stayed on the sidelines with an Equal-weight rating as valuation was seen leaving little room for error.
Bank of America is taking the long view on the restaurant stock. Analyst Sara Senator highlighted that Buy-rated Jersey Mike's

took more market share than any other chain in the limited-service sandwich categories, increasing its share of U.S. limited-service sandwich sales by 713 bps and share of units by 448 bps from 2018 to 2025. "The faster pace of sales share gains reflects growth that has been balanced between AUVexpansion and unit additions," she updated.

title: What analysts are saying about Jersey Mike's after its first earnings report
